newsitem.title: USA: Cigarette maker loses bid to move Florida trial.
newsitem.headline: Cigarette maker loses bid to move Florida trial.

text.p: Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp has lost a bid to shift a tobacco-liability case from the home base of the Florida attorney who last year scored the biggest courtroom victory against a cigarette company.
The B.A.T Industries Plc unit asked Florida's First District Court of Appeal to overturn the decision of a Jacksonville judge that the case stay in Jacksonville.
The tobacco company argued it would be more convenient for witnesses to testify in Palatka, some 40 miles from Jacksonville and near the home of plaintiff David Young, a smoker with lung ailments.

Brown & Williamson and other defendants, Brooke Group Ltd's Liggett Group and supermarket chain Winn-Dixie, also argued that Young did not fall ill in Jacksonville and that the city's courts should not be burdened with the case.

Young's attorney, Norwood Wilner, last year won a $750,000 verdict from a Jacksonville jury against Brown & Williamson on behalf of another smoker with lung disease. He is now alsoconducting a wrongful death trial in Jacksonville against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp. The appeal judges said in a written ruling dated April 4 that Jacksonville's courts could easily handle the case.
